source_refs.note: Exercise 3.3, Question 18: book p. 89-90, 24 questions (integration by parts); answer key p. 301 (printed under 'Exercise 3.5')

blocks.explanation:
Substitute \(t = \tan^{-1}x\) (\(x = \tan t\), \(1 + x^2 = \sec^2 t\)) to get \(\int e^t\cos^2 t\,dt\).
Plan: \(\cos^2 t = \frac{1 + \cos 2t}{2}\); \(\int e^t\cos 2t\,dt\) by parts twice; return to \(x\).
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{e^{\tan^{-1}x}}{(1 + x^2)^2}\,dx\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: substitute \(t = \tan^{-1}x\); reduce to \(\int e^t\cos^2 t\,dt\), use \(\cos^2 t = \frac{1 + \cos 2t}{2}\) and integrate \(\int e^t\cos 2t\,dt\) by parts twice.

Substitute \(t = \tan^{-1}x\)
\[x = \tan t,\ dx = \sec^2 t\,dt\]
\[(1 + x^2)^2 = \sec^4 t\]
\[= \int \dfrac{e^t\sec^2 t}{\sec^4 t}\,dt = \int e^t\cos^2 t\,dt\]
Why: \(1 + \tan^2 t = \sec^2 t\) and \(\frac{1}{\sec^2 t} = \cos^2 t\).

Reduce the power
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\int e^t\,dt + \dfrac{1}{2}\int e^t\cos 2t\,dt\]
\[= \dfrac{e^t}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}J\]
Why: \(\cos^2 t = \frac{1 + \cos 2t}{2}\); call \(J = \int e^t\cos 2t\,dt\).

Find \(J\) by parts twice
\[J = e^t\cos 2t + 2\int e^t\sin 2t\,dt\]
\[\int e^t\sin 2t\,dt = e^t\sin 2t - 2J\]
\[J = e^t\cos 2t + 2e^t\sin 2t - 4J\]
Why: trigonometric function first both times; \(\frac{d}{dt}\cos 2t = -2\sin 2t\), \(\frac{d}{dt}\sin 2t = 2\cos 2t\).

Solve for \(J\)
\[5J = e^t(\cos 2t + 2\sin 2t)\]
\[J = \dfrac{e^t}{5}(\cos 2t + 2\sin 2t)\]
Why: bring \(-4J\) to the left.

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{e^{\tan^{-1}x}(2x^2 + 2x + 3)}{5(1 + x^2)}\right] = \dfrac{e^{\tan^{-1}x}}{(1 + x^2)^2}\]
Why: verified by differentiation (sympy).
